task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 2, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style news update about Reedmile Parcel's rural-route contracting change and the tradeoffs facing drivers and customers.

facts.text: Reedmile Parcel announced Wednesday, Sept. 2, 2026, that three rural delivery zones will move to contractor Brack Lane Logistics on Oct. 19.
The three zones cover 1,460 delivery addresses; the count does not represent daily parcel volume.
Fourteen Reedmile drivers currently cover those zones within a wider workforce of 48 drivers.
Brack Lane has offered the 14 affected drivers route contracts that it describes as self-employed arrangements, not employee transfers.
The offered route fee is $168 for a completed route day, with drivers supplying their own vehicle, fuel and maintenance.
The offer does not guarantee a fixed number of route days every week.
Affected employee drivers currently receive $19 an hour and use company vehicles.
The record does not provide comparable route-hour or vehicle-cost data needed to calculate each driver's future net income.
Reedmile has also advertised two internal warehouse vacancies to affected drivers, with applications still open.
The company has not announced how many drivers accepted contracts, applied internally or intend to leave.
Reedmile says retail delivery charges and the promised delivery-day window will not change when contracting begins.
Customer complaints and compensation requests will still go through Reedmile rather than directly to individual drivers.
Driver Tavi Holt currently borrows a family car outside work and does not own a suitable parcel van.
Holt said, "A route fee starts looking different when the van has to come out of it."
Reedmile operations director Mara Venn said lower parcel density makes its rural routes more expensive per stop.
Venn said, "We are changing who runs the route, not asking customers to find a new parcel company."
Brack Lane has not published a route-by-route schedule or a guaranteed fuel adjustment in the offers supplied.
The reporting record contains no court or regulator determination of the proposed drivers' employment status.
Reedmile began serving the rural zones in 2019 after acquiring a smaller carrier.
The company has not released an independently assessed service-quality comparison between its current crews and the new contractor.

forbidden_additions: An employee transfer, accepted offers or guaranteed weekly contract income
A legal status ruling or a calculated net-pay reduction without hours and vehicle costs
